- `TasksTabScope`: `#description`, `#rows`, `#details`, `#chain-steps`.
- `RightSidebarScope`: `#tabs`, `#showing`.
- `PromptEditor`: `#basic-design-and-layout`, `#previous-tasks`, `#previous-task-filters`, `#chained-tasks`.
- `QueueListScope`: `#placement`.
- `MessageList`: `#scrolling-past`.

## Concept
### Pitch
The right sidebar's Tasks tab: every task of the project at a glance, what has run, what is running, and what is queued, where any of them can be looked into, edited, and adjusted, and a chain given more steps.
### Shape
#### Description
The tab is one scrolling column, with a [ScrollbarScope](../../scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope), read top to bottom as a timeline, in three groups, each headed by a small muted label with its count: "Previous", every task that has run, oldest at the top, as the [PromptEditor](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/index.md#prompt-editor)'s previous tasks are, with their filters and batch actions along the group's heading; "Running", every task under way, in either lane; and "Queued", the queue, in its order, as the [QueueListScope](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/queue-list/index.md#queue-list-scope) says, reordered by dragging, its auto-send switch and "Send next" button along its heading. A group with nothing in it shows its heading alone, muted, "No queued prompts" and the like. Each time the tab is shown, it is scrolled so the Running group, or the start of the Queued one when nothing runs, is in view.
#### Rows
Every task is one row, 28 pixels tall, as a queued prompt's is: a bar 2 pixels wide down its left edge in its mode's colour, as the [PromptModesScope](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) colours it, then its status, a spinner while it is under way, a tick, cross, or dash once it has ended, or, queued, its place in the queue, then the first line of its prompt, cut off with an ellipsis, then, at its right, muted, how long it took, or has been running, as the [MessageList](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list) writes it. A chain is one row, its steps as rows indented beneath it, collapsed to start with, as the previous tasks group a chain. Clicking a row opens it, as below, and the row stays highlighted while it is open. Hovering a row shows its prompt's first lines in its tooltip.
#### Details
An open task takes the tab's place, with a back arrow and the task's mode and name along its top, the arrow and <Escape> going back to the list as it was left. Opening a task that has run or is running also shows its output in the [MessageList](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list), as it shows the selected task, with a bar above it reading "Back to the latest task" while it isn't the latest. What the open task shows, top to bottom:
- At a glance: its status and how long it took, its lane, its place in the queue while it waits, the conversation it carries on or that it starts a new one, its model and effort, and once it has run, how many tool calls it made, its errors, its tokens and their cost, and how many files it changed, each a labelled figure, those that don't apply left out
- Its prompt, as it was typed, in a GrowingTextInputScope, and beneath it what is attached to it
- Its parameters: its mode, its model and effort, its Slice toggle, and whether it starts a new conversation, each as the chat input shows it
- Its actions: Resend, Send to Spec or Send to Code, Cancel while it is under way or queued, and Open output, as the PromptSendingScope gives them
A queued task is edited right there: its prompt can be typed in, its attachments removed, and its parameters changed, its mode among those of the tabs, a change of lane moving it to that lane's queue in its place. Each change is saved with the project as it is made, as saving a queued prompt's edit is, and while it is being changed the task is held, never sent, as a queued prompt being edited is; going back, or opening another, lets it go. A task that has run, or is running, can't be changed: its prompt and parameters read as they were sent, and "Edit and resend" puts them in the open task as a new queued prompt, ready to change, sent once "Send" is clicked. The chat input's own <Up> editing still works as the [ChatInputScope](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says, and opens the same task here.
#### Chain Steps
An open Chain task lists its steps beneath its parameters, in the order they run, each a row as in the list, with its status: its spec step, its code step, and its spec follow-up when it has one. An "Add step" button beneath them adds a step of its own after the last: a Code or a Spec step, chosen from a small menu, with a prompt of its own, typed in the step's row as it expands, its model and effort those of the chain until changed. An added step runs once the step before it finishes, in its own mode's lane and place, as every step of a chain does, told its own prompt, the chain's prompt as typed, and what the step before it replied, as the spec-to-code prompt tells a code step, so a chain can be carried on, as a further code change once the spec is built, or a spec tidy-up after the code. A step not yet sent can be edited, moved among the others not yet sent, or removed; one sent reads as it was. Steps are saved with the chain, in its hidden anchor, as the [PromptSendingScope](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) keeps a queued prompt, so a chain keeps its added steps across restarts, and a step whose step before it failed or was cancelled is never sent, as none of a chain's are.

1:# Right Sidebar Scope
3:## How To Build
7:## Theme
11:## Side
15:## Width
19:## Min Width
23:## Panels
29:## Sidebar
35:## Concept
37:### Pitch
41:### Shape
43:#### Description
48:#### Tabs
52:#### Resizing Panels
57:#### Look
63:#### Showing
#### Tabs

Along its top, a row of two tabs, as the body's tab bar draws tabs, 32 pixels tall: "Run" and "Tasks". Run holds its panels, the referenced files, the understanding, and the subagents, of the task selected in the message list, as above. Tasks holds the [TasksTabScope](./tasks/index.md#tasks-tab-scope): the queue and the previous tasks, which no longer sit in the message list. While a task runs, Run is selected as it starts, unless Tasks was picked since the sidebar last slid out; while none does, Run is disabled, its tooltip saying no task is running, and Tasks is shown. The tab picked is kept while the application runs, and each tab keeps its own scroll.

#### Showing

It is there while a task is running, from the moment a task is sent from the Code, Chain, or Spec tab until its run is over, and while the queue holds a prompt, and whenever it is opened by hand: a small ghost button with a sidebar icon at the right end of the body's tab bar, or Ctrl+Alt+B (Cmd+Alt+B on macOS), opens it on its Tasks tab, and closes it again, its tooltip saying which. Opened by hand, it stays until closed by hand, whatever runs; otherwise it slides back once nothing runs and nothing is queued. Questions from the Ask tab never show it, even when one is sent from the queue.
When a task starts, it slides out from the right edge of the message list and the chat input, growing from nothing to its width, its contents sliding into view from behind that edge as it does. When the run is over, it slides back the same way. The slide is quick and settles without bouncing. It pushes rather than covers: from the first frame of the slide to the last, the body's tab bar, the message list or open file beneath it, and the chat input end exactly at the sidebar's left edge, narrowing as it grows and widening as it shrinks, laid out again each frame, as the [BodyScope](../../../scope/application/Body.md#body-scope) says. Nothing runs beneath the sliding sidebar, nothing is clipped by it, and nothing jumps to a new width once the slide settles.

#### Basic Design And Layout

The [MessageList](./message-list/index.md#message-list) fills the body's Chat tab: all the space between the body's tab bar and the [ChatInputScope](./chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) along the bottom. #### Chained Tasks

A prompt sent in Chain runs as steps, each saved in the history as a task of its own: first the Chain task itself, which writes the spec; then the same prompt sent to Code, told what the spec step did; and, when the chain asks for a post-build spec update, the same prompt sent to Spec once more, told what the code step did. Each step knows the one it was sent from, as the [PromptSendingScope](./sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says. Only the steps the chain sends itself belong to it; a task sent to the other mode by hand, or resent, from one of its steps is a task of its own.
Each step runs in the lane of the work it does, as the [PromptSendingScope](./sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says: the Chain task and its spec follow-up in the spec lane, the code step in the code lane. A step is sent once the step before it finishes, never before, and takes its place in its lane's queue by when its chain was sent, not when the step itself was: behind every prompt waiting there that was sent before its chain, earlier chains' steps included, and ahead of every prompt sent after it. So a chain's code step never jumps ahead of a Code prompt, or another chain's code step, sent before the chain was, and a Code prompt sent while the chain's spec step ran waits for the chain's code step rather than coming between the chain's steps. Two steps whose chains were sent in the same order run in that order, whichever spec step finished first. Where nothing sent before its chain is waiting, it runs as soon as its lane is free, and straight away if it already is. Its place holds however it came to be queued, so a restart, with the queue read back from the project, keeps it there. The lane it leaves is free for its own queue meanwhile, so a Spec task sent while a chain's code step runs runs beside it. A step waiting for its lane shows in the queue like any prompt, and can be cancelled there, ending the chain. A step whose chain step before it failed or was cancelled is never sent.
Each step also runs where the work of its lane runs, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says: the spec steps in a container holding the spec and no code, the code step always on the host, with its protected locations. Each carries on its own lane's conversation, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says, so a step is told what the step before it did only through its prompt: the Chain prompt as typed and that step's final output, as the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](./mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope) says.
In the previous tasks list, a chain's steps are grouped under one parent item, so they read as parts of a single chain. The parent is a heading row in the list, tinted the Chain colour, as the [PromptModesScope](./modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) colours it, a little more strongly than a single task's tint: a joined chain icon, the first line of the prompt, and at its right how many steps it has, "2 steps" or "3 steps". Its status is the chain's as a whole: Running while any step runs, Failed or Cancelled if a step was, and otherwise that of its last step. It has no checkbox, Resend, or Send to the other mode of its own, and clicking it doesn't open anything.
Beneath it, each step stays an item of its own, exactly as any previous task is, with its checkbox, status, Resend, and whatever else a task offers, opening onto its own prompt, table, and changed files. The steps are indented from the parent, joined to it by a thin line in the Chain colour down their left, from the parent's heading to the last step, and each is labelled by what it did, "Spec", "Code", or "Spec follow-up", in that step's mode colour, before its prompt, which leaves out the prompt's first line when it is the parent's. They are listed in the order they ran.
A chain is listed where its first step was sent, oldest first like every other item; tasks sent while it ran, such as questions or tasks of the other lane run between its steps, are never listed within it, and are listed after the chain, in the order they were sent. A chain's steps are found by which step each was sent from, not by being next to each other in the history. A chain still running, or one whose later steps haven't been sent yet, shows as many steps as have been, and a step still running shows as it would anywhere. When the latest task, heading the view, is a step of a chain, that chain's earlier steps are still grouped under its parent in the list, the parent saying the rest is the latest task. A session divider never falls between a chain's steps: it goes above the chain's parent. A step from the history whose chain can't be worked out, as when the step it was sent from is missing, is listed as a task of its own.

#### Placement

The queue sits in the right sidebar's Tasks tab, its Queued group, as the [TasksTabScope](../../../ui/components/right-sidebar/tasks/index.md#tasks-tab-scope) says, never above the chat input or in the message list. Its heading says how many prompts are queued, and lists each queued prompt in order, one line each, with a button to cancel it. Each prompt in the list is numbered, with its number, text, and cancel button vertically centred in its row, and the list scrolls once it gets tall, with a [ScrollbarScope](../../../ui/components/scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope).
Every row is one line, 28 pixels tall, whatever its prompt holds: the prompt's first line of text, the first that isn't blank, in small text, cut off with an ellipsis where it doesn't fit, never wrapped, and never the rest of the prompt. A prompt with more lines than that shows nothing more in its row, and one with images attached shows a small muted image icon with how many, as "2", after its text, never the images themselves. So every row is the same height, and the list shows as many prompts as it has room for. Its tooltip gives the prompt's first few lines, as typed. Clicking the row's text, or anywhere in the row but its grip, switch, and buttons, edits the prompt in the chat input, as its pencil button does, as the editing below says: the whole prompt drops down into the input's editor, its tab selected, ready to change. A press that turns into a drag, from the grip, reorders rather than edits. Each time it is expanded, it opens scrolled to the bottom, on the prompts queued most recently, however it was scrolled when last closed. The same area holds the auto-send switch and the "Send next" button.
Editing a queued prompt from the chat input's <Up>, as the [ChatInputScope](../chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says, expands the list while the queue holds more than one prompt, scrolled so the prompt being edited is in view, following it as <Up> and <Down> move the edit along the queue. Once the edit is saved or cancelled, a list it expanded collapses again; one already expanded stays as it was. The queue is shown only while it has anything in it.

##### Scrolling Past

The previous tasks are not above the latest task in the message list but in the right sidebar's Tasks tab, so nothing lies past either end of the selected task's output: scrolling stops at its top and its bottom, with no stretch, glow, or crossing over. A task opened from the Tasks tab shows its output in the selected task's place, with a bar above it reading "Back to the latest task", which brings back the selected task's output scrolled just where it was left, its lock to the bottom as it was, as <Escape> in the message list does too.

8887	    fn render_queue(&self, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> Option<AnyElement> {
8888	        let count = self.queue.len();
8889	        if count == 0 {
8890	            return None;
8891	        }
8892	        let theme = cx.theme();
8893	        let (border, muted, background) = (theme.border, theme.muted_foreground, theme.tab_bar);
8894	        let expanded = self.queue_expanded;
8895	        // A prompt waits for "Send next" once its lane is free.
8896	        let lane_free = self
8897	            .queue
8898	            .iter()
8899	            .any(|item| !self.working.overlaps(Lanes::of(item.mode)));
8900	        let next_ready = self.next_sendable().is_some();
8901	        let controls = {
8902	            h_flex()

8904	                .px_4()

8906	                .child(

8910	                        .icon(if expanded {
8911	                            IconName::ChevronDown
8912	                        } else {
8913	                            IconName::ChevronRight
8914	                        })
8915	                        .label(format!("{count} queued"))
8916	                        .on_click(cx.listener(|this, _, _, cx| {
8917	                            this.queue_expanded = !this.queue_expanded;
8918	                            // Expanded or collapsed by hand, it stays so.
8919	                            this.queue_expanded_by_up = false;
8920	                            // It opens on the prompts queued last.
8921	                            if this.queue_expanded {
8922	                                this.queue_scroll.scroll_to_bottom();
8923	                            }
8924	                            cx.notify();
8925	                        })),
8926	                )
8927	                .child(div().flex_1())
8928	                .when(lane_free, |row| {
8929	                    row.child(
8930	                        Button::new("send-next")
8931	                            .primary()
8932	                            .small()
8933	                            .label("Send next")
8934	                            .disabled(!next_ready)
8935	                            .on_click(cx.listener(|this, _, _, cx| this.send_next_clicked(cx))),
8936	                    )
8937	                })
8938	                .child(
8939	                    Switch::new("auto-send")
8940	                        .label("Send next automatically")
8941	                        .checked(self.auto_send)
8942	                        .on_click(cx.listener(|this, auto_send: &bool, _, cx| {
8943	                            this.set_auto_send(*auto_send, cx)
8944	                        })),
8945	                )
8946	        };

8948	        // Where each prompt is and whether it is saved, for telling where a
8949	        // dragged prompt may be dropped: it moves only past saved prompts.
8950	        let saved: Rc<Vec<(usize, bool)>> = Rc::new(
8951	            self.queue
8952	                .iter()
8953	                .map(|item| (item.id, item.saved.is_some()))

mkdir -p /tmp/ed && cat > /tmp/ed/rm_items.py <<'EOF'
import sys, re
path = sys.argv[1]
names = sys.argv[2:]
src = open(path).read()
lines = src.split('\n')

def find_item(name):
    # name forms: "fn foo", "struct Foo", "enum Foo", "const FOO", "static FOO", "impl Foo"
    kind, ident = name.split(' ', 1)
    pats = {
        'fn': re.compile(r'^(\s*)(pub(\([^)]*\))? )?(async )?fn ' + re.escape(ident) + r'\b'),
        'struct': re.compile(r'^(\s*)(pub(\([^)]*\))? )?struct ' + re.escape(ident) + r'\b'),
        'enum': re.compile(r'^(\s*)(pub(\([^)]*\))? )?enum ' + re.escape(ident) + r'\b'),
        'const': re.compile(r'^(\s*)(pub(\([^)]*\))? )?const ' + re.escape(ident) + r'\b'),
        'static': re.compile(r'^(\s*)(pub(\([^)]*\))? )?static ' + re.escape(ident) + r'\b'),
        'impl': re.compile(r'^(\s*)impl(<[^>]*>)? ' + re.escape(ident) + r'\b'),
    }[kind]
    hits = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if pats.match(l)]
    if len(hits) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(f"{name}: {len(hits)} matches {hits}")
    start = hits[0]
    indent = len(lines[start]) - len(lines[start].lstrip())
    # extend upward over doc comments and attributes
    s = start
    while s > 0 and (lines[s-1].strip().startswith('///') or lines[s-1].strip().startswith('#[') or lines[s-1].strip().startswith('//')) and (len(lines[s-1]) - len(lines[s-1].lstrip())) == indent:
        s -= 1
    # find end: for const/static single statement ending with ';' at depth 0
    depth = 0; e = start; seen = False
    for i in range(start, len(lines)):
        l = lines[i]
        # strip strings crudely
        code = re.sub(r'"(\\.|[^"\\])*"', '""', l)
        code = re.sub(r"'(\\.|[^'\\])'", "''", code)
        code = code.split('//')[0]
        for ch in code:
            if ch in '{([': depth += 1; seen = True
            elif ch in '})]': depth -= 1
        if seen and depth == 0 and (code.rstrip().endswith('}') or code.rstrip().endswith(';') or code.rstrip().endswith('},') ):
            e = i; break
        if not seen and code.rstrip().endswith(';'):
            e = i; break
    # remove trailing blank line
    if e + 1 < len(lines) and lines[e+1].strip() == '':
        e += 1
    return s, e

for name in names:
    s, e = find_item(name)
    del lines[s:e+1]
open(path, 'w').write('\n'.join(lines))
print("removed", len(names))
EOF

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   Each user turn is a Suspense chain "code step" with a `<task-instructions>` block. The rules are:
   - Change ./src so it does what the compiled spec (.claude/reference) says.
   - Never read or edit ./spec. A deny rule blocks it, including via git diff or cat.
   - When the work is about Suspense, read .suspense/suspense-fluency.md once.
   - Before the first change, write the constraints once to the named `.suspense/history/<id>.understanding.md`. It is a Markdown list only, at most 12 lines, each linking to a compiled reference anchor.
   - End with a reply of a few sentences saying what changed, and mention where the spec and prompt disagree.

   Earlier completed tasks this session:
   - StopServerOnButtonClick2; NodeServerStuckRunning2; CollapsePromptsToSingleLine2; ReduceExcessiveHoverPopovers2; ShowPreviousTaskDurations2.
   - LeanTaskExecutionDefaults; ImplementDebugInfoCollection2; AddSpecCodeReadingOption2; CollapsePromptsLockSentButton2.
   - ExpandCodeReadingToProjectRoot2; AddTextWrapButton2; AddModelSelectionToChatInputScope2; AddEffortLevelSetting2.
   - EditorScopeHardWrapAt80Columns2: new src/piton_wrap.rs; the soft-wrap preference was removed.
   - BuildWithLatestGrammar: no change needed, the vendored grammar is already the latest.

   CURRENT task (understanding file `.suspense/history/1791569998-Prompt_c342193356262bc7.understanding.md`, already written). The prompt: "I think the @{RightSidebarScope} needs to be tabbed, and I think it needs a new tab -- and that's where the Queue should live, as well as previous tasks. When you click one you should be able to edit it, but this is also where you'd be able to adjust various parameters of it and see what's going on at a glance. And for multi-step prompts (like chain) you should even be able to add additional prompts."

   Spec anchors:
   - TasksTabScope `#description`, `#rows`, `#details`, `#chain-steps` (.claude/reference/ui/components/right-sidebar/tasks/index.md).
   - RightSidebarScope `#tabs`, `#showing`.
   - PromptEditor `#basic-design-and-layout`, `#previous-tasks`, `#previous-task-filters`, `#chained-tasks`.
   - QueueListScope `#placement`; MessageList `#scrolling-past`.

   What those anchors require:
   - The sidebar has Run and Tasks tabs, 32px tall.
   - The sidebar shows while a task runs, while anything is queued, or when opened by hand (a button at the body tab bar's right end, or Ctrl+Alt+B / Cmd+Alt+B on macOS).
   - The Tasks tab is a timeline of Previous / Running / Queued groups. Rows are 28px, with a mode-colour bar, status, first line, and duration.
   - Clicking a row opens details in the tab: glance figures, prompt, parameters, actions. A queued task is editable in place and held while open; a sent task offers "Edit and resend".
   - Chain tasks get "Add step" (Code or Spec), saved in the chain's hidden anchor.
   - The message list holds only the header and output, with a "Back to the latest task" bar; there is no scroll-past crossing.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Rust gpui / gpui-kit (gpui-component 0.6.1, gpui-base 0.6.1). TabBar has `suffix`; Tab has `disabled` and `tooltip`.
   - `DropdownMenu::dropdown_menu_with_anchor`, `PopupMenuItem::{new, element, checked, on_click}`.
   - `TextareaState::new(window,cx).auto_grow(1,N).default_value(..).placeholder(..)`, `Textarea::new(&state)`, `InputEvent::Change`.
   - ScrollHandle with `scroll_to_top_of_item` and `set_offset`; `DragScroll::driver(handle, vertical, row, entity_id, choose)` for drag auto-scroll.
   - Hidden anchor source/parse format with escape blocks (`push_block` / `read_escaped`).
   - Chain steps: `chain_next`, `chain_layout`, `chain_on`, `chain_holds`.
   - Tests: TestAppContext, `window.find` / `try_find` (requires test_support), `gpui_kit::TestSupportExt::test_support`. Entity leak detection forbids holding strong entities in thread_locals.
   - Helper /tmp/ed/rm_items.py removes Rust items (fn/struct/enum/const/static) by name with their doc comments. It aborts without writing if any name doesn't match exactly once.

3. Files and Code Sections:

     - Types: `SidebarTab {Run, Tasks}`, `Opened {Task(usize), Queued(usize)}`, `QueuedEditor`, `StepEditor`.

content.text:
The right sidebar now has Run and Tasks tabs, and the queue and previous tasks live in Tasks instead of the message list. The full suite passed on its last two runs (562 passed, 1 ignored, plus one new test that passes on its own), and clippy shows no new warnings.

- **Tasks tab:** one scrolling timeline grouped into Previous, Running and Queued. Previous keeps its filters and batch actions; Queued keeps drag reordering, auto-send and "Send next". The main code is in `src/prompt_mode/tasks_tab.rs`.
- **Clicking a task** opens it in the tab with its figures, prompt, settings and actions, and shows its output in the message list with a "Back to the latest task" bar. A queued task can be edited there, its mode, model, effort, attachments and slicing included; it saves as you go and isn't sent while open. A task that has already run offers "Edit and resend".
- **Chain tasks** get "Add step" (Code or Spec, with their own prompt, model and effort). Steps can be reordered or removed, are saved in the chain's hidden anchor, and run after the step before them.
- **Showing the sidebar:** it slides out while a task runs or anything is queued. A button at the right end of the body tab bar or Ctrl+Alt+B (Cmd+Alt+B on macOS) opens or closes it by hand.
- **Removed:** the old scroll-past list and the queue above the chat input.

I also fixed three bugs along the way:
- The Tasks list grew to fit its content instead of scrolling.
- Closing the sidebar by hand while a task ran reopened it on the next frame.
- A task sent while an older one was open left that older one marked as being viewed.

Several tests had to change because they relied on the old list.

**Where the spec and prompt disagree:**
- **Clicking a queued row:** the queue list's spec says it edits the prompt in the chat input, but the Tasks tab's spec says it opens the task in the tab. I followed the Tasks tab and kept the pencil button for editing in the chat input.
- **Ask tasks:** the sidebar's spec says it shows "while a task runs", but I kept the existing rule that a running Ask question doesn't open it.

**Limits:**
- Steps can only be added to a chain that has been sent, not to one still queued.
- If the chain has already finished, a "Send step" button runs the new step.
- The old session dividers and per-group actions are gone.
- The drag-to-scroll test failed once during the full runs and passed every run after that, so it may be timing-sensitive.
